title: Licence Application Form for Intermediaries
text:
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMMISSION
INSURANCE ACT, 2021 (ACT 1061)
APPLICATION FOR INSURANCE INTERMEDIARY’S LICENCE
(Insurance Broker, Reinsurance Broker, Technical Service Provider,
and Insurance Loss Adjuster)
1. Name of Applicant ……………………………………………………………………………..
2. Location of Registered Office of Applicant………………………………………….................
.…………………………………………………………………………………………………
3. Postal Address, E-mail Address, Telephone Number (s) and Digital Address
…………………………………………………………………………………………………..
…………………………………………………………………………………………………..
4. State the category of licence for which application is made ……….…………………………..
.………………………………………………………...........................………………………..
5. In the case of a Technical Service Provider, state
a) Name of Insurer(s) in partnership with…………………………………………………………..
b) Name of Telco(s) in partnership with ……………………………………………………………
6. State whether any of the parties connected with this application have ever applied, individually or in
conjunction with others, for authority to transact insurance or other financial services business in any
other jurisdiction and, if so, provide full details.
7. State any jurisdiction(s) outside Ghana in which the applicant carries on, or is proposing to carry
on, business as an insurance intermediary.
8. Details of professional indemnity insurance effected or to be effected, including insurer and level of
cover. (A minimum of GH¢200,000 for (Re)Insurance Broking/Loss Adjusting Companies and
GH¢500,000 for Technical Service Providers).

DECLARATION BY APPLICANT
We hereby apply for a licence and declare the above particulars to be true and correct and agree to notify the
National Insurance Commission of any material alteration to the foregoing information supplied, and that,
(a) we have not been adjudged insolvent or bankrupt
(b) we have not made any assignment or any arrangement or composition with creditors which has
been rescinded or set aside, and
(c) we have not been convicted by a court of an offence involving dishonesty, fraud or gross
misconduct, nor have had to appeal against conviction by the terms of any enactment in force in
Ghana or any other country.

Signature………………………………………………...

Signature………………………………….. Signature………………………………………………..

For use of National Insurance Commission only
Action Taken Date
Date received:…………………. 1. Acknowledged: .. ….………….
Fee Paid:…………………… 2. Further Enquiries: ..……………..
Receipt No:…………………. 3. Decision: ..……………..
ENCLOSURES TO THE APPLICATION
1. Copies of company registration documents from the Registrar General’s Department.
2. Detailed curriculum vitae, completed Personal Questionnaire and Personality Notes Form from all
Shareholders, Directors and Principal Officers.
3. A detailed Business Plan containing estimated setting up costs and relevant projections.
4. Evidence of availability of minimum capital and its source.
5. Copies of all contracts regulating applicant’s relationship with other companies, transferring the
applicant’s functions to other companies and any other contracts the contents of which influence the
financial situation of the applicant.

6. If applicant is a company, the following must be attached.
(a) The names (including any previous name), addresses and nationalities of all persons exercising control
over the applicant, e.g. shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners of shares in the company;
(b) Where shares are beneficially owned by a corporate body, or the company is part of a group, the chain
of connection (group organization chart showing all associated and affiliated companies) to the ultimate
owners must be provided;
(c) The directors and principal officers of the applicant, showing their respective positions with the
applicant.
7. Particulars and letters of consent from the applicant’s auditor.
8. The latest Audited Statement of Affairs of the applicant.
9. Evidence of professional indemnity cover.
10. Description of the office location to be approved by the Commission.
11. Application fee.
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FOR TECHNICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS
1. Copies of Partnership Agreements must be submitted.
2. A Technical Service Provider has the liberty to enter into partnership with unlimited number of Insurance
Companies, both life and non-life insurance companies to sell microinsurance products, subject to approval by
the NIC.
3. Applications for licensing of Sub-Agents and Trainee Agents (newly recruited agents) to sell microinsurance
products are required to be presented to the NIC by an Insurer. The licensed agent can sell for the insurer that
presented him for licensing. Meanwhile, the agent can sell for one life and one non-life insurance company. But
both companies must present the agent for licensing.
4. A Technical Service Provider, shall submit to the NIC on semi-annual basis, and in a format determined by the
NIC, a report containing the number of policies sold during the year by product type and the premiums generated.
The report shall be submitted within four (4) weeks after the end of June and December.
5. Sections 109-134 and all other provisions of the Insurance Act 2021 (Act 1061) Regulations, Market Conduct
Rules, Code of Practice and Guidelines, which apply to insurance intermediaries shall apply to Technical Service
Providers as well.
6. A corporate body cannot be the agent for its own insurances.
